production_notes: [VERSION] Record the screen demo only after checking the live tools: interfaces, model names, the image option in Gemini, aspect-ratio controls, the Firefly content-type setting, number of images per request, download options, free-tier limits and generative credits for Gemini, Google AI Studio and Adobe Firefly all change often. Update the screen_steps if menu names differ.
[VERIFY] Whether each tool adds visible or invisible AI labels to downloaded images must be confirmed (see L10). The voiceover only says that some tools add labels.

Scene 15 (Compare): the presenter names two real differences seen in the recorded results. The voiceover gives lighting and how much counter is visible as examples; re-record the line if the live results differ.
Use a demo Google account and a demo Adobe account with no personal data visible. Blur account names, email addresses and any credit balance tied to a real person.
Efua and her Accra bakery are fictional; no real bakery names or logos in the prompts or images.

Hook.voiceover: You now know how to write a strong prompt. Today, you will put the same prompt into two different tools, and watch them produce two different images. By the end, you will know where the main controls are.

Explain.voiceover: This course uses two generators that you can start with for free: Gemini and Adobe Firefly.

slide.title: Your First Images in Gemini and Firefly
slide.body: AI Image Generation and Visual Design · Lesson 3 of 12 · Screen demo

Explain.voiceover: Gemini is Google's AI assistant. You create images by chatting. You write a request, see the result, then ask for changes in plain language, like make the background lighter. Google AI Studio is a more technical Google workspace with more settings, and you can use it as an alternative.

slide.title: Gemini
slide.body: Create images by chatting · Ask for changes in plain language: 'make the background lighter' · Alternative: Google AI Studio, more settings

Explain.voiceover: Adobe Firefly is Adobe's image tool. It works more like a control panel. You write a prompt, then choose settings from menus, such as aspect ratio, content type, photo or art, and style effects. The free tier gives you a limited number of generative credits.

slide.title: Adobe Firefly
slide.body: Prompt box plus a settings panel · Aspect ratio · Content type: photo or art · Style effects · Free tier: limited generative credits

Explain.voiceover: So what is the difference for a beginner? In Gemini, you change images through conversation, and you often ask for the aspect ratio in the prompt. In Firefly, you use buttons and menus. Each tool also has its own default look. And some tools add labels that show an image was made with AI. We come back to that in lesson ten.

slide.title: Gemini vs Firefly
slide.body: Two columns. Gemini: changes by conversation · aspect ratio written in the prompt · its own default look. Firefly: buttons and menus · aspect ratio from a menu · its own default look. Footer: some tools add AI labels (see L10).

Explain.voiceover: Gemini is like asking a helpful assistant to draw for you, and giving feedback as you talk. Firefly is like working at a studio desk with labelled switches. Both can produce good work. They simply feel different to use.
Explain.stock_query: designer desk with control panel switches

Explain.voiceover: One safety note before we start. While you practise, do not upload photos of real people, client files or anything confidential. Use your own simple prompts.
Explain.on_screen_text: No real people or client files

Demonstrate.voiceover: Let's make an image for Efua, who runs a small bakery in Accra, Ghana. You can read the prompt on screen. It asks for a wooden tray of sugar bread and meat pies on a bakery counter, as an eye-level product photograph with soft warm light, in golden brown and cream.

slide.title: Efua's bakery prompt
slide.body:
A wooden tray of freshly baked sugar bread loaves and meat pies on a bakery counter,
product photograph, eye-level close-up, soft warm light from the left,
golden brown and cream colours with a small green plant in the background

Demonstrate.voiceover: We start in Gemini. I open it in the browser and sign in with a Google account. I start a new chat, and if there is an image option in the tools menu, I select it. Then I paste the prompt and add one sentence: make it a square, one to one image.
screen_steps: Open Gemini in a web browser and sign in with a Google account
Start a new chat
If there is an image option or tool menu, select image creation
Paste the bakery prompt and add: 'Make it a square 1:1 image.'
Press send
Demonstrate.on_screen_text: Gemini: ask for the shape in words

Demonstrate.voiceover: Here is the result. Look at the details from the prompt. The tray, the loaves, the warm light from the left, and the small green plant. Now I type a follow-up. Keep everything the same, but make the background slightly darker.
screen_steps: Wait for the result
Point out which details from the prompt appear: tray, bread, meat pies, light from the left, green plant
Type the follow-up: 'Keep everything the same, but make the background slightly darker.'
Press send

Demonstrate.voiceover: The background is darker, and the bakes stand out more. That is the Gemini way. You improve the image by talking to it. When I am happy, I open the image and use the download option to save it.
screen_steps: Show how the image changed after the follow-up
Open the image
Use the download option to save it

Demonstrate.voiceover: Now Adobe Firefly. I open the Firefly website, sign in with a free Adobe account, and choose text to image. I paste the same prompt, but without the sentence about the aspect ratio, because here we use the settings panel instead.
screen_steps: Open the Adobe Firefly website and sign in with a free Adobe account
Choose the text-to-image option
Paste the same prompt, without the aspect-ratio sentence

Demonstrate.voiceover: In the panel, I set the aspect ratio to square, and the content type to photo. Notice the credit counter. Each generation uses credits, so plan your prompt before you click. Now I click generate.
screen_steps: In the settings panel, set aspect ratio to square (1:1)
Set content type to photo
Point out the credit counter, if visible, and explain that each generation uses credits
Click Generate

Demonstrate.voiceover: Here are the Firefly results. I hover over the best one and download it. Now let's place both images side by side and compare.
screen_steps: Hover over the best Firefly result
Download it
Place the Gemini image and the Firefly image side by side

Demonstrate.voiceover: Two differences stand out here. The lighting feels different in each image, and one tool shows more of the counter than the other. Neither is simply better. The right choice depends on what Efua's bakery needs.
screen_steps: With both images side by side, point to the difference in lighting
Point to how much of the counter each image shows
Name the two differences out loud

Demonstrate.voiceover: A common mistake is to decide that one tool is better after one test. Every generation is random, so compare several results against your brief. And do not spend all your free credits on quick experiments.

slide.title: Avoid these mistakes
slide.body: One test tells you very little: compare several results · Judge against your brief, not your first impression · Plan the prompt first, then spend credits

Recap.voiceover: Let's recap. First, Gemini works through conversation, while Adobe Firefly works through a panel of settings like aspect ratio and content type. Second, the same prompt gives different results in different tools, so judge them against your brief. Third, free tiers have limits that change often, so plan before you generate.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Gemini = conversation · Firefly = settings panel. 2. Same prompt, different results: judge against the brief. 3. Free tiers have limits: plan before you generate.

CTA.voiceover: Now it is your turn. In the exercise below, you will create one image for the Accra bakery in both tools from the same prompt, and note two differences. It takes about twenty minutes. In the next lesson, we explore composition, lighting and colour words. See you there.
CTA.on_screen_text: Next: Composition, Lighting and Colour Words
